author: blu
body: Format is positional S-expressions: every node is a paren-delimited list whose first element is a tag atom. Strings are double-quoted with backslash escapes for backslash, double-quote, and newline. Identifiers are bare atoms. Spans are elided -- the plug fills synthetic-span on parse since downstream emitters don't read span.

author: blu
body: Surface AST type expressions. Distinct prefix from CodexType atoms ("a" prefix) so a parser can tell them apart structurally.

author: blu
body: The expression printer. Each variant fits a single (atom ...) form. Type tags follow the structural arguments -- match the IRExpr constructor order so a parser can read positionally.

author: blu
body: This walk collects the names a definition REACHES. It used to collect every name-shaped thing it passed -- text literals, let names, param names, field names, pattern variables, error messages -- on the reasoning that over-collecting only ever keeps too much. That is true of soundness and false of usefulness: a compiler writes its own function names as text literals (runtime helper names, builtin names, diagnostics), and a field or a parameter routinely shares a name with some definition somewhere. On the compiler's own source the walk retained essentially everything and the prune was inert -- measured, before this change: zero definitions dropped out of 5167.

author: blu
body: If this list is ever wrong, the build says so and names the definition: every call, address-of and effect-op slot is checked at finalize and an unresolved one raises CDX2040 and refuses the binary.

author: blu
body: The multi-root form. A root naming no definition is skipped rather than refused -- ir-dce-add-name already answers -1 for a name the index does not hold -- so a caller may offer a root that only some programs carry. The FIRST root is different: if it is absent the chapter comes back whole, because a chapter with no entry point is one we cannot reason about and must not prune. That is the rule the single-root form has always had, and the IR-text callers depend on it.

author: blu
body: A punctual definition that declares an EXPLICIT budget and does not survive the prune is a budget nothing checks. The instruction count is taken per emitted body (emit-all-defs), so a definition the inliner absorbed into its callers, or one nothing ever calls, reaches emit-wcet-check never and both CDX6010 and CDX6011 go silent. Measured against seed EFC7FCD0: a five-instruction body declaring a budget of two raises CDX6011 with the inliner off and nothing at all under the default pipeline, so the declared budget was unenforced in the shipping configuration and the author had no way to tell.

author: blu
body: It takes two def LISTS and not two chapters, and that is the whole correctness of it. ir-prune-roots-flood ends in `__record-set m "defs"`, which stores into the field and hands back THE SAME record, so the chapter a caller passed in and the chapter it got back are one object. Written to take chapters, this function compared the pruned list against itself, every name matched, and it reported nothing on a program whose budget was demonstrably being dropped. The caller must therefore bind the def list BEFORE calling the prune. The old list is safe to hold: ir-dce-filter builds a fresh one and `__record-set` only swaps the field.

author: blu
body: The arms are nested rather than joined with `&` so the bounds test guards the subscript by control flow. A conjunction would leave `list-at kept j` reachable at j equal to the length whenever the last definition in the chapter is the pruned one.

author: blu
body: Top-level entry. Plug parsers expect a single (chapter ...) form on input. Strings list-fields use a "(strs ...)" wrapper for consistency.

author: blu
body: Prose blocks and annotations ride the chapter header so that per-def prose survives the wire. A block prints as its anchor and its text; the classification is re-derivable from the text and is not sent. An annotation prints as kind, target, body. Plug parsers walk the header by form name and skip forms they do not ask for, therefore both forms are additive.

author: blu
body: The same walk with the name printed BEFORE the render and the size after, so a def that cannot be rendered at all is named by the last line that survives. It exists because "peak heap is the largest single def" above is a design statement with no instrument behind it: on the compiler's own source the whole-compiler `-IrCce` emit dies before `SIZE:` is printed, which puts the cost in this pass, and nothing said WHICH def. Reached with `compile.ps1 -IrCce -RawFlags "wsz"`.

author: blu
body: Not folded into `ir-defs-wire-size`: that one is on the shipping path and pure, and giving it a Console effect to carry a diagnostic would put the effect row on every caller.

author: blu
body: It was written to test a hypothesis that `list-push` copies and makes this quadratic, and it REFUTED it: 1.48 MB across all 5,201 definitions of the compiler's own source, largest 32,784 bytes, and the per-def figures are capacity-doubling rather than quadratic. The DCE collection is not a cost. Kept because that is worth being able to re-establish in one run.
